# 239. CLAUDE / LLM ANNOTATION CONTRACT AND PRODUCTION PROMPT PACK

## 239.1 Frozen master system instruction

```text
ROLE
You are the annotation and data-curation engine for the CulinaryState computational gastronomy research dataset.
You are NOT a recipe author and NOT an authority allowed to invent missing scientific values.

PRIMARY TASK
Transform REAL source recipes and VERIFIED external evidence into strict structured records while preserving raw text, provenance, uncertainty, missingness and the distinction between observed facts and inferred/modelled information.

NON-NEGOTIABLE SCIENTIFIC RULES
1. NEVER invent a missing quantity, temperature, pH, duration, chemical concentration, physical property, sensory property, intermediate state, mechanism or process condition.
2. UNKNOWN is valid and preferred when evidence is absent.
3. Every nontrivial field uses one of:
   EXPLICIT_SOURCE
   EXTERNAL_VERIFIED
   DERIVED_DETERMINISTIC
   INFERRED_LLM
   MODEL_ESTIMATED
   IMPUTED
   SIMULATED
   UNKNOWN
4. Never promote INFERRED_LLM, MODEL_ESTIMATED, IMPUTED or SIMULATED to observed/gold evidence.
5. Preserve exact raw source text/spans alongside normalization.
6. Food identity, form, state, process, quantity, unit, size, role and intermediate identity are different variables.
7. A surface string is not automatically a new canonical concept.
8. Do not create a new canonical concept if an existing concept plus modifiers explains the phrase.
9. Deterministic unit conversion is performed by the unit engine, not guessing.
10. Volume/count-to-mass conversion requires ingredient/form/packing/locale-specific evidence; otherwise leave mass UNKNOWN.
11. Count portions such as egg, clove, fillet, bunch, slice or head require a portion profile before mass conversion.
12. Do not average pH values to estimate mixture pH.
13. Do not infer compound concentration from ingredient presence alone.
14. Do not infer process chemistry from a generic cooking action without approved scientific evidence.
15. Recipe procedure/state graph is not chemistry ground truth.
16. Preserve conflicting evidence and create a conflict record; do not silently choose one value.
17. Preserve qualifiers: about, approximately, heaped, packed, level, divided, optional, to taste, reserve, drained, peeled, cooked, raw, etc.
18. Split, merge, reserve, discard, reuse and recombine operations are explicit graph operations.
19. All production outputs conform exactly to the supplied schema.
20. Do not add prose outside the schema in production calls.

CANONICALIZATION
FOOD: resolve aliases to canonical food IDs where justified; keep variety/cultivar/form/state separate.
QUANTITY: separate scalar/range/fraction/count/qualitative amount and uncertainty.
UNIT: map to internal unit IDs and physical standards when valid; preserve locale ambiguity.
SIZE: small/medium/large are modifiers, not masses.
FORM: whole/sliced/diced/chopped/minced/ground/powdered/grated/crushed/julienned etc.
STATE: raw/cooked/frozen/thawed/dried/roasted/boiled/softened/browned/caramelized/fermented etc.
PROCESS: use canonical process ontology; do not create synonyms as separate processes.
INTERMEDIATE: create a new entity when transformation/combination creates a meaningful downstream mixture/state.
COREFERENCE: resolve it/them/mixture/remaining/half/reserved only when supported; otherwise unresolved.
CONDITIONS: temperature, time, pH, pressure, moisture, medium and endpoint are independent fields.
ENDPOINT: until-golden/until-tender are state/stop observations, not hidden numeric conditions.

PROVENANCE
Every normalized field retains source span or external evidence reference, extraction pass, provenance class, model/prompt/schema version and uncertainty/missingness.
```

## 239.2 Ingredient/vocabulary extractor prompt

```text
Extract every ingredient mention.
Preserve raw phrase and span.
Resolve food head to existing canonical ingredient ID if possible.
Extract quantity, raw unit, size, variety, form, state, packing, optional/divided/reserved qualifiers separately.
Return candidate IDs when ambiguous.
Propose TRUE_NEW_CONCEPT only when no existing concept + modifiers can represent the phrase.
Never invent weights or scientific properties.
```

## 239.3 Vocabulary curator prompt

```text
For each proposed vocabulary addition, compare existing concepts/aliases and classify:
EXISTING_ALIAS
EXISTING_CONCEPT_WITH_MODIFIERS
TRUE_NEW_CONCEPT
AMBIGUOUS
POLYSEMOUS
COMPOUND_FOOD
BRAND
NON_FOOD
HUMAN_REVIEW
If TRUE_NEW_CONCEPT, create an internal canonical record and optional external ontology mappings.
Never create a concept merely for spelling, quantity, cut, state, size or preparation modifier.
```

## 239.4 Quantity parser prompt

```text
Parse exact raw quantity expression into scalar/range/fraction/count/unit/size/container/packing/qualitative/approximate/optional/divided/reserved fields.
Do NOT perform food-specific gram conversion.
Do NOT infer missing quantities.
Preserve phrases such as to taste, as needed, pinch, dash, handful, splash and enough to cover as qualitative unless the task explicitly uses an evidence-backed distribution.
```

## 239.5 Quantity grounding prompt

```text
Resolve a parsed quantity using this order:
1 exact deterministic physical conversion
2 exact authoritative food-specific portion record
3 authoritative density record
4 multi-source food-specific portion estimate
5 empirical corpus distribution
6 otherwise UNKNOWN
Record the method/source/uncertainty.
Never use common-sense guessing where an approved lookup is absent.
```

## 239.6 Event parser prompt

```text
Parse instructions into atomic events with process, inputs, outputs, tools, medium, explicit time, explicit temperature, other explicit conditions, endpoint/state phrases and source spans.
Split compound instructions when multiple actions/conditions/outputs exist.
Represent merge, split, reserve, discard, reuse, transfer, rest, cool, heat, mix and recombine explicitly.
Create intermediate entities where needed.
Do not infer chemistry.
```

## 239.7 State reconstructor prompt

```text
Using only parsed entities/events plus explicit observations, construct the procedural state graph.
Track identity, parents, quantity if known, location, form, qualitative state, thermal state and process history.
Do not fabricate quantitative chemical state.
Every state field has a provenance class.
```

## 239.8 Quality reviewer prompt

```text
Audit without rewriting.
Check missing ingredients, wrong entity merges, vocab mistakes, impossible conversions, mass/volume confusion, unresolved coreference, lost quantities, split/merge allocation, fabricated conditions/chemistry, contradictory states, missing event inputs/outputs, duplicate canonical concepts and provenance violations.
Return only PASS / PASS_WITH_WARNINGS / REANNOTATE / HUMAN_REVIEW plus machine-readable validation flags.
```

## 239.9 Scientific evidence researcher prompt

```text
Given food/state/process/target, locate primary or high-quality scientific evidence.
Extract only measured values, conditions, units, matrix, analytical method and exact source provenance.
Return UNKNOWN if no suitable measurement exists.
Distinguish raw composition, processed composition, kinetic evidence and mechanistic evidence.
Do not transform absence of evidence into a numeric estimate.
```

## 239.10 Production prompting rules

- Use frozen prompt IDs and hashes.
- Include 3–5 difficult representative examples per task, not only easy examples.
- Use strict structured output / schema validation.
- Separate passes rather than one mega-call: structural parse → canonicalization → state graph → quantity grounding → QA → optional evidence enrichment.
- Log model/provider/version/settings for every batch.
- Reprocess old Silver only under explicit dataset-version migration; never silently mix annotation policies.
- Use cheaper specialized models for routine extraction after distillation; reserve stronger LLM/human review for hard cases.

# 240. QA, VALIDATION, ACTIVE LEARNING, AND SPARSITY-AWARE CONSTRUCTION

## 240.1 Validation stack

```text
V1 schema/JSON
→ V2 ontology/ID constraints
→ V3 arithmetic/unit/quantity checks
→ V4 temporal graph/state consistency
→ V5 semantic reviewer/model disagreement
→ V6 human adjudication for queued cases
```

## 240.2 Canonical validator rules

- JSON parses and exactly matches declared schema version.
- All referenced IDs exist.
- No event consumes an entity before it exists.
- Every new intermediate has a producing event.
- Every split/merge relation has consistent parent/child references.
- Every EXPLICIT_SOURCE field has a source span.
- Every EXTERNAL_VERIFIED field has an evidence/source reference.
- Every normalized quantity has a conversion route or remains unknown.
- Dimensional unit arithmetic is valid.
- No count portion is converted to mass without a food-specific portion record or empirical distribution.
- Ranges remain ranges in source/gold objects.
- Qualitative quantities are not silently numericized.
- Locale-sensitive units preserve locale/ambiguity.
- No chemistry value appears from a recipe-only annotation pass.
- No pH/water-activity value appears unless explicit/external/model/simulated provenance is declared.
- Model-estimated/imputed/simulated fields are excluded from observed-gold target tables.
- Duplicate-group members remain in the same final split.
- Gold test/calibration rows are human verified according to policy.
- LLM-extracted scientific rows entering final evaluation are human verified.
- Source lineage prevents multiple copies of one study from counting as independent evidence.
- Unit/target definitions are harmonized before contradiction declaration.
- Current state can be replayed from event history.
- Vocabulary concept creation does not duplicate existing alias + modifiers.
- High-frequency unresolved terms are added to review queue.
- Annotation/model/prompt/schema versions are present.
- Source checksum is present for reproducibility.
- License/redistribution status is recorded when source text may be released.
- No final response factual claim lacks evidence/model provenance in the claim ledger.
- Abstention/qualitative downgrade activates outside calibrated support.
- FlavorTwin sensory-equivalence wording is blocked without sensory evidence.


## 240.3 Active-learning review priority

Use uncertainty/disagreement, mention frequency, vocabulary novelty, downstream importance, source diversity and coverage gaps to prioritize human review. Humans should spend time on high-impact ambiguous cases rather than easy random examples.

## 240.4 Sparsity policy

100k recipes will still be sparse in temperature, pH, water activity and chemistry. That missingness is measured and reported; it is not filled by LLM guesses. Maintain masks and separate scientific evidence/model/simulation planes.

## 240.5 Observation propensity

Because measured food-process chemistry is MNAR, missing cells can reflect popularity, analytical method, publication practice and detectability. Completion/propensity methods remain Level-15 research objects and never convert missingness into observed truth.


# 241. RETRIEVAL, RERANKING, EVIDENCE COMPATIBILITY, CONFLICT, AND CONTEXT RESTRUCTURING

## 241.1 Multi-stage retrieval

```text
R1 structured hard/soft filters
R2 lexical/BM25
R3 dense semantic retrieval
R4 graph/evidence expansion
R5 cross-encoder reranking
R6 state/process/condition/target compatibility
R7 dedup + lineage + conflict analysis
R8 evidence packet compilation
```

## 241.2 Candidate fusion

Union structured, lexical and dense candidate pools. Reciprocal-rank fusion is a useful baseline because it avoids pretending incomparable retriever scores are calibrated probabilities.

## 241.3 Compatibility vector

For evidence candidate \(E_j\):

\[
m_j=[m_{food},m_{state},m_{process},m_T,m_t,m_{pH},m_{target},m_{matrix},m_{measurement},m_{source}].
\]

Preserve categorical match types such as EXACT, SAME_SPECIES, SAME_FOOD_GROUP, SAME_PROCESS_FAMILY and GENERIC_MECHANISM before learning any scalar compatibility score.

## 241.4 Hard negatives

Retrieval training/evaluation must include scientifically close hard negatives: same food wrong process, same process wrong time/temperature, same target related food, raw vs processed mismatch, wrong analytical endpoint. Pure semantic negatives are too easy.

## 241.5 Contradiction workflow

Before declaring a genuine contradiction:

1. harmonize units/metric definitions;
2. check food/cultivar/matrix;
3. check state/form;
4. check process leaf/family;
5. check conditions;
6. check analytical platform;
7. check source lineage/independence;
8. check evidence tier/quality.

Only then create a conflict cluster.

## 241.6 Context packet compiler

Compile by reasoning role, not retriever rank. Include direct facts/evidence, near evidence, mechanisms, model estimates, conflicts, unknowns, feasible actions and disallowed claims with citation map.

## 241.7 Table/figure evidence

Preserve table row/column headers, caption, unit and footnotes. Plot-digitized values are labeled DIGITIZED with extraction uncertainty rather than treated as exact tabular measurements.


# 242. CONFIDENCE, CALIBRATION, EVIDENCE SUFFICIENCY, AND ABSTENTION

## 242.1 Confidence vector

Do not start with `confidence = 0.83`. Maintain interpretable dimensions:

\[
\mathbf q=[q_{retrieval},q_{entity},q_{quantity},q_{process},q_{condition},q_{target},q_{source},q_{measurement},q_{extraction},q_{agreement},q_{state},q_{model},q_{OOD}].
\]

## 242.2 Separate confidence tasks

Potentially calibrate different probabilities:

- evidence supports query;
- entity link is correct;
- quantity conversion is within tolerance;
- citation supports generated claim;
- transition prediction lies within tolerance;
- proposed action is feasible;
- final response mode should answer vs abstain.

## 242.3 Calibration data

Use independently verified Deep-Gold/calibration data. Avoid circular labels produced by the same model whose confidence is being calibrated.

## 242.4 Calibration models

Start simple: logistic/Platt/isotonic or small calibrated tree models. A huge opaque confidence model is not automatically better.

## 242.5 Metrics

Report Brier score, ECE/reliability plots, error-detection AUROC/AUPRC and risk–coverage.

## 242.6 Evidence sufficiency modes

```text
DIRECT / FULL SUPPORT
NEAR / PARTIAL SUPPORT
MODEL-SUPPORTED INTERPOLATION
BROAD QUALITATIVE SUPPORT
IRRELEVANT EVIDENCE
NO EVIDENCE
CONFLICTING EVIDENCE
```

## 242.7 Output precision policy

High evidence → quantitative when target definition supports it.  
Moderate evidence → interval/range/ordinal.  
Low but meaningful evidence → qualitative.  
Unsupported/conflicting beyond resolution → abstain or explicitly report conflict.

\[
\boxed{output\ precision\le evidence\ precision}
\]

## 242.8 Decision cascade

```text
DIRECT EVIDENCE
→ supported interpolation
→ calibrated Level-15 model estimate
→ broad qualitative evidence
→ abstain
```

Imputed/simulated values may assist internal models but cannot masquerade as direct evidence.


# 243. DECISION POLICY, CANDIDATE ACTIONS, DIAGNOSIS, RECOVERY, AND VALUE OF INFORMATION

## 243.1 Decision modes

\[
M_t\in\{ANSWER,COMPARE,ASK,DIAGNOSE,RECOVER,RECOMMEND,ABSTAIN\}.
\]

The policy receives current state, history, goals, constraints, evidence packet and uncertainty.

## 243.2 Candidate action generation

Generate structured candidates from the process ontology, recipe/state corpus, evidence/rules, Level-15 transition/inverse models and optionally an LLM proposer. The LLM may propose; structured evidence/constraints verify.

## 243.3 Feasibility before utility

Every action checks required tool, medium, state prerequisites, time, sequence and explicit user constraints before outcome ranking.

## 243.4 Candidate record

Each candidate stores action/conditions/stop criterion, predicted outcome, evidence route, evidence class, uncertainty, OOD/support distance, feasibility and goal-match vector.

## 243.5 Multi-objective decisions

Do not silently choose weights for browning, nutrition, time, uncertainty, effort or sensory preference. Return Pareto/trade-off alternatives unless the user supplies a priority or a task-specific objective is justified.

## 243.6 Diagnosis

Generate candidate causes, then verify each against observed symptoms, process history, supporting/contradicting evidence and missing discriminating observations. Cause language is qualified unless controlled evidence warrants causality.

## 243.7 Recovery

Cause evidence and recovery evidence are distinct. Recovery seeks an acceptable reachable state; it may recognize REVERSIBLE, PARTIALLY_REVERSIBLE, CONTAINABLE, IRREVERSIBLE or UNKNOWN recoverability.

## 243.8 Information-gathering actions

`ASK`, `OBSERVE`, `MEASURE` are valid actions. Ask only when an observation has meaningful expected decision value.

Conceptually:

\[
VOI(x)=U_{before}-E[U_{after\ observing\ x}]
\]

with user burden/query cost considered.

## 243.9 Stop conditions

Prefer state-based stop criteria (golden edges, target texture, visible simmer) where appropriate rather than fixed time alone. Endpoint phrases are invalid leakage when used as future-label inputs during training, but valid execution-time stopping observations.

## 243.10 Receding-horizon interaction

```text
recommend one supported step
→ user/sensor observes
→ state graph updates
→ evidence/transition recomputed
→ next step
```

This is more defensible than autonomous whole-recipe planning under sparse dynamics.

## 243.11 Practical POMDP interpretation

The theoretical framing is partial observability, but the semester implementation uses state estimate + uncertainty + VOI questioning + short-horizon action rather than a full POMDP/RL system.


# 244. RUNTIME / SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

## 244.1 Recommended service decomposition

```text
raw-source registry
schema/vocabulary service
quantity/portion engine
semantic parser service
recipe-state graph service
scientific evidence ledger
lexical/dense retrieval indexes
structured/graph retriever
compatibility/reranker
Level-15 transition service
decision/diagnosis/recovery service
claim/citation verifier
LLM response interface
evaluation/reporting harness
```

## 244.2 Storage strategy

Relational storage for canonical IDs, quantities, events, states, evidence and provenance.  
Vector index for semantic passages/evidence atoms/recipe text.  
Lexical index for exact scientific/ingredient/process terms.  
Graph relations may be relational adjacency tables first; a graph database is optional, not required.

## 244.5 Versioning

# 245. LEVEL-16 BENCHMARK, ABLATIONS, AND END-TO-END EVALUATION

## 245.1 Benchmark families

| Family | Primary target |
|---|---|
| SEM | ingredient/action/state semantic parsing |
| LINK | canonical food/process/entity linking |
| QTY | quantity structure and grounding |
| GRAPH | recipe entity/event/state graph |
| RET | evidence retrieval |
| EVID | evidence compatibility/conflict/lineage |
| CONF | calibration, sufficiency and abstention |
| TRANS | Level-15 transition fallback |
| DEC | next-action/compare/ask/abstain policy |
| DIAG | diagnostic hypothesis generation/verification |
| REC | recovery action quality/recoverability |
| FT | FlavorTwin retrieval/inverse search |

## 245.2 Semantic metrics

Span precision/recall/F1 for FOOD, QUANTITY, UNIT, FORM, STATE, TOOL, ACTION, DURATION and TEMPERATURE. Macro reporting is required.

## 245.3 Entity linking

Acc@1, Recall@5, hierarchical/category accuracy and OOD alias/source performance.

## 245.4 Quantity metrics

Exact quantity-structure match plus mass/volume error only on authoritative ground truth. For distributional predictions report interval coverage and interval width.

## 245.5 Graph metrics

Node F1, edge/relation F1, merge/split F1, coreference accuracy, event-order accuracy and replay consistency.

## 245.6 Retrieval metrics

Recall@K, MRR, NDCG plus **condition-compatible Recall@K** and exact-target/source-level diagnostics.

## 245.7 Citation/provenance metrics

Citation precision, citation recall, claim-evidence entailment/manual verification and unsupported-claim rate:

\[
UCR=\frac{unsupported\ factual\ claims}{all\ factual\ claims}.
\]

## 245.8 Sufficiency/abstention

Build cases with direct support, partial/near support, irrelevant evidence, no evidence and genuine conflict. Evaluate decision-mode F1 and risk–coverage.

## 245.9 Decision metrics

Action Recall@K, feasibility/violation rate, mode F1, goal-state error where measurable, and decision consistency under equivalent paraphrases/units.

## 245.10 Clarification/VOI benchmark

Compare NeverAsk, AskEverything and VOIAsk using downstream decision quality and number/user-cost of questions.

## 245.11 Diagnosis/recovery metrics

Hypothesis Recall@K, evidence support, useful-next-test rate, recovery validity, recoverability classification and transition toward acceptable state.

## 245.12 Baseline ladder

```text
B0 LLM only
B1 dense RAG
B2 BM25 + dense hybrid RAG
B3 structured metadata RAG
B4 state-aware RAG
B5 state + evidence compatibility/conflict packet
B6 + Level-15 transition fallback
B7 + calibrated recommend/ask/abstain decision layer
```

## 245.13 Mandatory ablations

Remove one at a time:

- state reconstruction;
- quantity grounding;
- structured retrieval;
- evidence compatibility;
- conflict/lineage processing;
- transition fallback;
- uncertainty/OOD gate;
- feasibility filtering;
- provenance/claim ledger.

A module that adds no measurable value should not be retained merely for architectural elegance.

## 245.14 Oracle cascades

Evaluate downstream modules with oracle state/evidence and predicted state/evidence. The gap localizes error propagation.

## 245.15 Robustness tests

- semantic paraphrase invariance;
- exact unit invariance (C↔F, kg↔g);
- correct locale sensitivity for ambiguous units such as cup;
- state sensitivity (pale vs already dark);
- constraint sensitivity (oven vs pan only);
- goal sensitivity (maximize vs minimize browning);
- evidence sensitivity (direct evidence should replace model-only mode);
- source-disjoint/cold ingredient/process evaluation.


# 246. FLAVORTWIN V2 — PRESERVED BOUNDARY AND SHARED CORE

## 246.1 Scope decision

FlavorTwin remains in the project, but **do not expand its conceptual architecture further before implementation of the shared Level-16 state/evidence/quantity core**. The current boundary is sufficient for the course plan.

## 246.2 Target factorization

\[
Z^*=\{Z_{chemical},Z_{sensory},Z_{functional},Z_{process},Z_{culinary}\}.
\]

Do not define one universal flavor-similarity scalar.

## 246.3 Search hierarchy

```text
target
→ retrieve plausible ingredients
→ static/structural/sensory/culinary baselines
→ process expansion
→ condition refinement where supported
→ recipe-role/context reranking
→ evidence/OOD/constraint gate
→ diverse Pareto candidates
```

## 246.4 Candidate identity

\[
\boxed{candidate=ingredient+state+process+conditions}
\]

when process evidence exists. Static candidate baselines remain mandatory.

## 246.5 Contextual substitution

\[
score(i\rightarrow j\mid recipe,role,process,quantity).
\]

A substitution can require quantity or process compensation, but such compensation is model/evidence dependent and cannot be invented.

## 246.6 Evidence classes

```text
OBSERVED_MATCH
STRUCTURAL_MATCH
SENSORY_SUPPORTED_MATCH
MODEL_ESTIMATED_MATCH
PROCESS_SIMULATED_MATCH
EXTRAPOLATED
UNSUPPORTED
```

## 246.7 Permanent sensory boundary

\[
\boxed{chemical\ similarity\neq perceived\ flavor\ equivalence}
\]

Strong sensory-equivalence claims require sensory/human validation.

## 246.8 Evaluation boundary

Retain random/category/ECFP/descriptors/static embeddings/static multiview/process-conditioned/process+recipe-context baselines. Process conditioning earns complexity only if it improves a held-out process-sensitive task beyond uncertainty and without unacceptable OOD/constraint violations.

## 246.9 Shared core

CulinaryState-RAG and FlavorTwin share canonical foods, quantities, state graph, process ontology, evidence ledger, transition engine, uncertainty/OOD and provenance. Project A is forward/decision; Project B is target/inverse search.

# 247. RESEARCH QUESTION PORTFOLIO — 30 EXECUTABLE R&D QUESTIONS

## 247.1 RQ16-01 Semantic state value

**Question / hypothesis:** Does explicit culinary-state reconstruction improve evidence retrieval and next-action decisions over query-text-only RAG?

**Data required:** Deep Gold state/action cases + evidence benchmark.

**Baseline/control:** B2/B3 hybrid RAG without state.

**Proposed method:** state-aware retrieval + decision.

**Headline split:** source/duplicate-disjoint.

**Metrics:** ConditionCompatible@K, ModeF1, UCR.

**Promotion criterion:** promote state module only if improvement persists beyond bootstrap CI.

**Main risk / alternative explanation:** state parser errors may erase gain.

**Decision use:** a positive, null or negative result is retained and changes the next architecture step; the experiment is not repeated until the desired architecture wins.

**Metrics:** Recall@K, citation precision, UCR.

**Main risk / alternative explanation:** over-filtering under sparse evidence.

**Decision use:** a positive, null or negative result is retained and changes the next architecture step; the experiment is not repeated until the desired architecture wins.

# 248. EXPERIMENT PORTFOLIO, HYPOTHESIS CARDS, AND PAPER-FLOW

## 248.1 Experiment families

### E16-A — Semantic parsing benchmark
Gold spans/entities/relations; compare rules, smaller encoders, LLM extraction, distilled parser and hybrid verifier.

### E16-B — Quantity benchmark
Quantity parsing, canonical units, authoritative portion grounding, interval coverage and downstream quantity encoder ablations.

### E16-C — Vocabulary/cold-start benchmark
Alias linking, modifier factorization and cold source/region/ingredient evaluation.

### E16-D — Recipe graph benchmark
Intermediate nodes, coreference, merge/split/reserve/discard/recombine, event order and next-state prediction.

### E16-E — Evidence retrieval benchmark
BM25, dense, hybrid, structured, state-aware and compatibility-reranked retrieval with scientific hard negatives.

### E16-F — Evidence packet / grounded generation
Raw chunks vs structured packet; measure citation correctness, unsupported claims, conflict handling and answer mode.

### E16-G — Confidence/abstention
Self-confidence vs calibrated feature models; risk–coverage and support-regime tests.

### E16-H — Decision policy
LLM-only vs state/evidence/feasibility/transition/VOI policy on next-action gold.

### E16-I — Diagnosis/recovery
Failure ontology and proposer-verifier vs generic troubleshooting.

### E16-J — Transition integration
Retrieval-only vs retrieval+gated Level-15 fallback on direct-missing but in-support queries.

### E16-K — FlavorTwin static→process-conditioned
Structural/static/multiview/process-conditioned/contextual baselines.

### E16-L — Full-system evaluation
Locked final test across factual, comparison, state, action, diagnosis, recovery, OOD and conflict scenarios.

## 248.2 Publication logic

Do not force all experiments into one paper. Potential publishable units:

1. **CulinaryState semantic corpus + CQPO** — dataset/annotation/quantity contribution.
2. **State- and evidence-aware culinary RAG** — retrieval/context/confidence/abstention contribution.
3. **Sparse process-state transition modeling** — Level-15 paper path.
4. **Process-conditioned FlavorTwin** — inverse-search/substitution paper if data and evaluation mature.

A course project may implement a subset while the SSOT preserves the larger R&D program.

## 248.3 Negative results policy

If simpler parsing, retrieval, LightGBM, direct evidence or static FlavorTwin baselines match more complex approaches, retain the simpler system and report the negative result. Complexity is not a deliverable.


# 249. LEVEL-16 PROMOTION GATES, STOP RULES, AND DECISION FRAMEWORK

## 249.1 Core gates

### G16-DATA
Deep Gold exists with independent annotation/adjudication; Silver quality and source/duplicate controls documented.

### G16-VOCAB
High mention coverage is achieved; high-frequency unresolved/ambiguous concepts below declared threshold; concept/alias fragmentation audited.

### G16-QTY
Deterministic units correct; food-specific portion conversions have provenance; qualitative/unknown quantities are not fabricated; interval calibration reported where distributional.

### G16-SEM
Ingredient/action/state/coreference parsers meet declared Deep-Gold thresholds and source-disjoint performance is reported.

### G16-GRAPH
Recipe graph temporal integrity, intermediate, merge/split and coreference metrics meet declared acceptance criteria.

### G16-EVID
Evidence retrieval has acceptable compatible Recall@K/citation support and preserves exact provenance.

### G16-CONFLICT
Conflicting evidence is detected/qualified rather than silently collapsed.

### G16-CAL
Confidence/abstention calibrated on held-out independent gold; risk–coverage reported.

### G16-TRANS
No Level-15 fallback is used for a target/domain until the relevant G15 gates pass.

### G16-DEC
Structured decision system reduces unsupported/infeasible actions relative to strong RAG baselines while maintaining useful coverage.

### G16-REC
Diagnosis/recovery relations are separately evidenced and recoverability uncertainty is explicit.

### G16-PROV
Every factual/scientific response claim is traceable to evidence or explicit model output.

### G16-OOD
Cold ingredient/process/source/condition behavior and abstention are measured.

### G16-FT
FlavorTwin process/context complexity is promoted only if it beats static baselines on process-sensitive held-out tasks.

## 249.2 Stop rules

Stop increasing complexity and invest in data/evidence when:

- Silver does not improve held-out Gold performance;
- canonicalization errors dominate parser errors;
- quantity conversions are mostly unsupported;
- structured retrieval does not beat strong hybrid RAG;
- confidence is uncalibrated under source shift;
- Level-15 model adds coverage but materially increases unsupported claims;
- feasibility rules remove too many gold-valid actions;
- diagnosis gold is too ambiguous for strong causal claims;
- process-conditioned FlavorTwin fails to beat static baselines;
- human verification cost exceeds the value of the proposed feature.

## 249.3 Architecture promotion order

\[
\boxed{
Rules/lookup
\rightarrow
strong\ simple\ baseline
\rightarrow
structured\ model
\rightarrow
learned\ model
\rightarrow
agentic/optimization\ layer
}
\]

No stage is skipped merely because the later stage sounds more novel.


# 250. DATA GOVERNANCE, LICENSING, REPRODUCIBILITY, COST, AND SECURITY

## 250.1 Source licensing

Record source license/terms/redistribution status. Do not assume that publicly viewable commercial recipe text can be redistributed as a public corpus. Where necessary release derived annotations/IDs/statistics rather than copyrighted full text.

## 250.2 Raw-source immutability

Store raw snapshots/checksums where permitted. Never overwrite source text with normalized text.

## 250.3 PII and comments

If using recipe comments/Q&A for failure/recovery mining, remove/avoid unnecessary personal information and retain only what is permitted by source/license/research protocol.

## 250.4 Reproducibility ledger

Every experiment records dataset hash/version, split registry, ontology version, prompt/model version, code commit, seeds, compute environment and evidence snapshot.

## 250.5 Annotation cost accounting

Track model tokens/calls, API cost, human review minutes, records per hour, validation failure rate and cost per accepted Gold-Light/Silver record. Optimize quality per cost, not raw throughput.

## 250.6 Model-provider independence

Schemas and provenance contracts are provider-neutral. Claude may be a primary annotation/research engine, but data format and validation do not depend on proprietary hidden state.

## 250.7 Release tiers

Potential release artifacts:

- fully redistributable canonical vocab/ontology;
- quantity/portion records permitted by source terms;
- derived recipe annotations linked to source IDs;
- gold benchmark text only where licensing permits;
- evidence atoms with citations rather than copyrighted full papers;
- code/prompts/validators/split registries.

# 251. RISK REGISTER AND FAILURE-MODE CONTROLS

| Risk | Failure mechanism | Observable consequence | Primary control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vocabulary explosion | synonyms/forms/states become separate concepts | coverage rises but semantic quality falls | alias clustering + modifier factorization + human review |
| Over-merging foods | distinct regional/functional foods collapsed | contextual errors and cultural loss | hierarchical concepts + ambiguity queue + regional review |
| Quantity false precision | counts/qualitative amounts forced to grams | downstream state/nutrition errors | portion evidence ladder + intervals + UNKNOWN |
| Locale unit ambiguity | cup/tablespoon meanings differ | systematic mass errors | locale field + ambiguity/no conversion when unresolved |
| LLM fabrication | missing T/pH/chemistry invented | contaminated scientific targets | master prompt + provenance validator + separate evidence plane |
| Gold anchoring | human accepts model suggestion | biased benchmark | independent annotation before seeing model output |
| Duplicate leakage | copied recipes across splits | inflated metrics | duplicate/source grouping before split |
| Source template leakage | parser learns website format | poor real generalization | source-disjoint benchmark |
| MNAR evidence bias | popular foods/processes dominate | misleading completion confidence | propensity/sensitivity + bucket reporting |
| Evidence lineage duplication | many pages cite same study | false consensus | lineage groups/dedup |
| Conflict collapse | system hides inconsistent science | overconfident answer | condition-aware conflict graph + explicit conflict mode |
| Retriever semantic shortcut | linguistically similar wrong condition | scientifically wrong citations | structured compatibility + hard negatives |
| Confidence theater | arbitrary 0–1 scores | misleading trust | feature vector + held-out calibration |
| Transition overreach | model predicts outside evidence | unsafe/unsupported recommendations | G15 gates + OOD + qualitative downgrade/abstain |
| Optimizer exploitation | inverse search finds model error | nonsensical FlavorTwin/process settings | evidence/support constraint + conservative objective |
| Procedure/chemistry conflation | recipe states treated as chemical truth | false mechanism claims | separate data planes and provenance |
| Sensory overclaim | chemical similarity called same flavor | invalid FlavorTwin claim | human/sensory boundary |
| Cascade errors | early parse error corrupts decision | hard-to-debug failures | module benchmarks + oracle upstream experiments |
| Cost blow-up | 100k multi-pass strong-model calls | project stalls | pilot scaling + distillation + tiered models |
| Scope creep | tries to add vision/RL/world model prematurely | core system unfinished | L17 deferred; promotion gates |


# 252. AUTHORITATIVE EXECUTION ROADMAP

## Phase 0 — freeze the contracts

Deliver schemas, ontology seed, quantity units, annotation handbook, master prompts, validators, manifest and split policy.

**Exit:** 100–500 difficult recipes can be represented without schema improvisation.

## Phase 1 — Deep Gold seed

Independent annotation/adjudication; quantify span/entity/quantity/event/state/graph agreement.

**Exit:** errors are understood and schema/prompt v1 is stable enough for pilot.

## Phase 2 — vocabulary + CQPO bootstrap

Mine high-frequency aliases, external ontology alignments and authoritative portion/density records. Build deterministic conversion engine.

**Exit:** high-frequency ingredients/units resolve reliably; conversion provenance works end-to-end.

## Phase 3 — 10k Silver pilot

Run multi-pass LLM annotation + validators. Do not scale further until audit.

**Exit:** validation failure rate, vocab growth, source bias and human-review workload are acceptable/documented.

## Phase 4 — Level-12/14/15 parallel evidence tracks

Run molecule/ingredient baselines and acquire process/chemistry evidence while recipe Silver scales. These tracks do not wait for 100k completion.

## Phase 5 — 25k → 60k Silver + Gold-Light active learning

Distill specialized parsers where useful; prioritize ambiguous/high-impact cases for human verification.

## Phase 6 — freeze recipe-semantic dataset v1

Potentially scale to 100k if gates justify it. Freeze duplicate/source-safe benchmark splits and dataset card.

## Phase 7 — L16 semantic retrieval/evidence compiler

Implement BM25+dense+structured retrieval, compatibility/reranking, lineage/conflict and evidence packets.

## Phase 8 — confidence + selective policy

Calibrate confidence/sufficiency on held-out gold; implement direct/interpolate/model/qualitative/abstain cascade.

## Phase 9 — decision/diagnosis/recovery

Implement structured candidates, feasibility, short-horizon transition fallback, VOI questions, failure/recovery knowledge base.

## Phase 10 — full CulinaryState-RAG benchmark

Compare B0–B7 and required ablations on locked test data.

## Phase 11 — FlavorTwin V2 implementation

Only after shared state/evidence/transition core is usable. Start with static baselines, then process/context conditioning.

## Phase 12 — optional future multimodal extension

Only if course/research time remains and the core system is empirically validated.

# 257. DEFINITION OF DONE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

The core R&D **specification** is done now. The **implementation** is done only when the following can be demonstrated reproducibly:

1. a raw recipe can be parsed into versioned ingredient/quantity/event/state objects without inventing missing science;
2. the current recipe/session state can be replayed from events;
3. quantity conversions show their evidence class and uncertainty;
4. aliases resolve to canonical foods while modifiers remain separate;
5. a Deep-Gold benchmark exists independently of Silver predictions;
6. source/duplicate-safe splits are frozen;
7. the retriever can find state/process/condition-compatible evidence and exact provenance;
8. context is compiled into direct/near/conflict/model/unknown/disallowed-claim sections;
9. confidence/abstention is calibrated on held-out gold;
10. Level-15 fallback is only invoked in validated domains;
11. candidate actions are feasibility checked before recommendation;
12. diagnosis/recovery separates cause from recovery evidence;
13. every factual response claim has traceable provenance;
14. strong RAG baselines are beaten or the simpler baseline is retained;
15. FlavorTwin static baselines are run before process-conditioned claims;
16. negative/null results are retained in the decision record;
17. all reported results can be rerun from dataset/split/code/model/prompt versions.


# 257A. OPERATIONAL ANNEX — COMPLETE LEVEL-16 DECISION TREES, TEST CASES, SOURCE POLICY, AND BUILD HANDBOOK

This annex is deliberately operational. It captures details that are easy to lose when the architecture is described only at a high level.

## 257A.1 Canonicalization decision tree for ingredient vocabulary

For every new ingredient surface phrase:

```text
STEP 1 — normalize typography only
  lowercase where language permits
  Unicode normalize
  normalize whitespace
  preserve original raw phrase separately

STEP 2 — parse modifiers
  quantity?
  unit?
  size?
  packing?
  variety/cultivar?
  form/cut?
  state/preparation?
  brand?
  geographic qualifier?
  compound-food phrase?

STEP 3 — remove non-identity modifiers conceptually
  search canonical vocabulary + alias table

STEP 4 — decide
  exact alias → EXISTING_ALIAS
  canonical + modifiers → EXISTING_CONCEPT_WITH_MODIFIERS
  multiple plausible concepts → AMBIGUOUS/POLYSEMOUS
  branded item representing ordinary food → BRAND_ALIAS / PRODUCT_VARIANT
  composite dish/ingredient → COMPOUND_FOOD
  genuinely distinct food concept → TRUE_NEW_CONCEPT
  not food → NON_FOOD

STEP 5 — external alignment
  search approved ontology/database mapping when useful
  preserve internal ID even if no external mapping exists

STEP 6 — provenance
  record first-seen source, frequency, locales, model/human decision
```

### 257A.1.1 Examples of factorization rather than concept explosion

```text
"large red onion, finely chopped"
  food = onion
  variety/color = red
  size = large
  form = finely_chopped

"roasted unsalted peanuts"
  food = peanut
  state = roasted
  salt_state = unsalted

"frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry"
  food = spinach
  source_state = frozen
  event/state history = thawed → squeezed_dry

"1 can diced tomatoes"
  food = tomato
  form = diced
  container = can
  quantity handled separately

"garlic cloves"
  food = garlic
  portion/count unit = clove
  do not create food concept "garlic clove" unless ontology design intentionally models anatomical portion as a child concept
```

### 257A.1.2 Canonical concept review triggers

Send a proposed concept for human review when:

- it occurs above a declared frequency threshold and remains unresolved;
- the phrase maps to two plausible foods with materially different composition/culinary role;
- it is culturally/regional specific and external ontologies disagree;
- it may be a branded product with formulation-dependent composition;
- it is a compound food whose decomposition would lose recipe meaning;
- it is a fermentation starter/culture with process-specific behavior;
- it is a preparation whose identity changes materially (e.g., stock, paste, concentrate) and cannot be represented as a simple state modifier.

## 257A.2 Quantity normalization decision tree

```text
INPUT: raw quantity phrase + ingredient + form/state + source locale

1 parse numeric structure
  exact scalar?
  fraction?
  range?
  count?
  qualitative?

2 resolve raw unit
  physical SI/imperial?
  culinary volume?
  count/portion?
  container?
  informal qualitative?

3 determine locale
  explicit source locale?
  dataset-level locale?
  unresolved?

4 deterministic conversion
  mass↔mass or volume↔volume with known physical unit
  if valid: DERIVED_DETERMINISTIC

5 food-specific conversion required?
  volume→mass
  count→mass
  container→mass
  size→mass

6 lookup hierarchy
  authoritative exact portion
  authoritative density
  other approved national table
  multi-source verified estimate
  empirical corpus distribution
  model estimate only if task explicitly permits

7 output
  exact value if authoritative/deterministic
  interval/distribution if variable
  UNKNOWN if unsupported
```

### 257A.2.1 Required quantity test expressions

The parser/validator suite must contain hard examples such as:

```text
1 cup millet
1 1/2 cups millet
1½–2 cups water
2 large eggs
2 eggs, beaten
1 (14 oz) can tomatoes
one 400 g tin tomatoes
1/2 bunch coriander leaves
3 cloves garlic
1/4 tsp ground cloves
one 6-ounce salmon fillet
juice of 1/2 lemon
zest of one lemon
1 heaped tbsp flour
1 level tablespoon cocoa
1 packed cup brown sugar
1 loosely packed cup herbs
a pinch of salt
a dash of bitters
a splash of milk
a handful of spinach
water as needed
oil for frying
salt to taste
flour for dusting
2 x 200 g chicken breasts
three 250-mL bottles
1 small onion
1 medium onion
1 large onion
half the reserved sauce
one third of the dough
remaining batter
```

Expected output for these tests is structural parsing plus evidence-grounded conversion status, not invented gram values.

## 257A.3 Process/action canonicalization decision tree

For an action phrase:

```text
surface phrase
→ identify head action
→ identify modifiers (intensity, geometry, granularity, medium, endpoint)
→ map to canonical process leaf
→ map leaf to process family
→ retain original phrase
→ create event with explicit inputs/outputs/conditions
```

Examples:

```text
"finely chop" → CHOP + granularity=fine
"roughly chop" → CHOP + granularity=rough
"pan fry" → FRY / PAN_FRY depending ontology granularity
"deep fry" → FRY + immersion=deep / dedicated leaf if justified
"simmer gently" → SIMMER + intensity=gentle
"bake until golden" → BAKE + endpoint=golden
```

Do not make `finely chop`, `roughly chop`, `chop coarsely` three unrelated process concepts unless an experiment explicitly requires separate canonical leaves.

## 257A.4 State field policy

Each state field has one of these states:

```text
KNOWN_EXPLICIT
KNOWN_EXTERNAL
DETERMINISTICALLY_DERIVED
INFERRED
MODEL_ESTIMATED
IMPUTED
SIMULATED
UNKNOWN
CONFLICTING
NOT_APPLICABLE
```

`UNKNOWN` and `NOT_APPLICABLE` are not the same. For example, pH may be unknown; `whole/sliced` may be not applicable to a liquid mixture depending on the schema.

## 257A.5 Scientific evidence acquisition hierarchy

For process/chemistry evidence, prioritize:

1. primary controlled experimental paper/table;
2. curated authoritative database retaining primary provenance;
3. systematic review/meta-analysis with extractable conditions;
4. high-quality review for mechanism/context only;
5. secondary source only as a lead to the primary source;
6. LLM knowledge is never a scientific evidence source.

For every quantitative scientific row capture:

```text
food/matrix
food state/form
process leaf/family
T/time/pH/moisture/pressure/medium where reported
target variable/compound
before/after or trajectory values
units/basis (wet/dry/yield-corrected etc.)
analytical method
replicates/sample information if available
study/source ID
exact table/figure/span
extraction method
human verification status
```

## 257A.6 Chemistry enrichment firewall

Recipe annotation may link a food to known external chemistry evidence, but it must not insert unsupported chemistry into the recipe state.

Allowed:

```text
recipe ingredient: tomato
external evidence: tomato contains compound X in database/source
link exists with EXTERNAL_VERIFIED provenance
```

Not allowed:

```text
recipe uses tomato
therefore exact compound-X concentration in this specific tomato batch = database average
```

Allowed model behavior:

```text
model estimate uses external prior with explicit uncertainty/model provenance
```

## 257A.7 Global/localization policy

The data factory should record, where available:

- source country/locale;
- language;
- measurement system;
- regional ingredient aliases;
- transliteration variants;
- cuisine labels as source metadata rather than assumed identity;
- locale-sensitive portion conventions.

Do not infer ethnicity/nationality from ingredient names. Cuisine/source labels are dataset metadata, not personal attributes.

## 257A.8 Multilingual extension boundary

English can be the first production language. Multilingual data should enter only when:

- schema is language-independent;
- canonical concepts are stable;
- language-specific alias tables exist;
- annotation evaluation exists for that language;
- machine translation is not silently treated as gold source text.

## 257A.9 Failure/recovery ontology starter

Suggested parent families:

```text
THERMAL
  burnt
  under_browned
  over_browned
  scorched
  undercooked
  overcooked

MOISTURE
  too_wet
  too_dry
  watery
  soggy
  over_reduced

EMULSION_PHASE
  split_emulsion
  curdled
  separated

TEXTURE_STRUCTURE
  tough
  mushy
  gummy
  grainy
  collapsed
  under_set
  over_set

FERMENTATION_LEAVENING
  under_proofed
  over_proofed
  weak_rise
  over_fermented

SEASONING_BALANCE
  too_salty
  too_sweet
  too_acidic
  too_bitter

PROCEDURAL
  wrong_order
  omitted_step
  incorrect_allocation
  insufficient_rest
```

Cause, symptom and recovery are separate relation types. A failure can have multiple causes and a cause can have multiple recovery options or no reliable recovery.

## 257A.10 Decision-mode examples

```text
"What does boiling do to X?" → ANSWER / PROCESS_EFFECT
"Should I steam or boil?" → COMPARE
"Why is this sauce watery?" → DIAGNOSE
"How can I fix it?" → RECOVER
"What should I do now?" → RECOMMEND
"Is the pan very hot or only gently simmering?" → ASK (information gathering)
unsupported exact chemistry request → ABSTAIN or QUALITATIVE
```

## 257A.11 Candidate-action schema checklist

Every candidate action should define, when applicable:

```text
action_type
canonical_process_id
target_entity_ids
condition changes
duration or stop criterion
tool requirements
medium requirements
state prerequisites
hard constraints
soft preferences
expected state effects
evidence/model route
evidence class
predictive interval
OOD/support distance
feasibility result
rejection reasons
goal-match vector
```

## 257A.12 Rejection reason registry

```text
MISSING_TOOL
MISSING_MEDIUM
INCOMPATIBLE_STATE
UNMET_PREREQUISITE
TIME_CONSTRAINT
USER_CONSTRAINT
NO_EVIDENCE
LOW_SUPPORT
HIGH_UNCERTAINTY
HIGH_OOD
MODEL_NOT_VALIDATED
DOMINATED_OPTION
RECOVERY_NOT_EVIDENCED
IRREVERSIBLE_STATE
UNKNOWN_STATE_CRITICAL
```

## 257A.13 Evidence packet anti-hallucination controls

The packet may include explicit `DISALLOWED_CLAIMS`, for example:

```text
DO NOT claim an exact pH.
DO NOT claim exact vitamin concentration.
DO NOT call model-completed values measured.
DO NOT call structural similarity sensory equivalence.
DO NOT infer causality from cross-study association.
DO NOT cite a review as the measured primary experiment when the primary source is available.
```

## 257A.14 Claim-language policy by provenance

```text
EXPLICIT / MEASURED:
  "The study measured..."

EXTERNAL_VERIFIED:
  "The referenced database/study reports..."

INTERPOLATED:
  "Based on nearby measured conditions..."

MODEL_ESTIMATED:
  "The model estimates..."

IMPUTED:
  "A completion model estimates an unmeasured cell..."

SIMULATED:
  "The simulator predicts under its assumptions..."

CONFLICTING:
  "The available evidence is inconsistent under comparable conditions..."

UNKNOWN:
  "The available evidence does not support a reliable estimate..."
```

## 257A.15 Source/duplicate split construction

Recommended order:

```text
1 normalize source IDs
2 compute exact duplicate hashes
3 detect near duplicates from title + ingredients + instructions
4 create duplicate families
5 identify source-domain/template families
6 assign groups before train/val/calibration/test split
7 freeze split registry
8 never move examples after looking at final test performance
```

## 257A.16 Data release/version semantics

A release should declare:

```text
dataset_version
schema_version
ontology_version
quantity_database_version
source_snapshot_date
annotation_model/prompt versions
human gold revision
split registry hash
license/redistribution notes
known limitations
```

## 257A.17 Compute and cost strategy

The project is predominantly data/evidence-limited. Cost optimization should follow:

```text
deterministic parser/regex/unit logic first
→ smaller semantic model for routine cases
→ stronger LLM for ambiguous cases
→ human only for high-value unresolved cases
```

Track:

```text
cost per raw recipe
cost per accepted Silver recipe
cost per human-verified Gold-Light example
human minutes per adjudicated Deep-Gold recipe
reannotation rate
validator failure rate
```

## 257A.18 Latency strategy for runtime RAG

Runtime should avoid performing every expensive operation synchronously.

Precompute/cache:

- canonical entity embeddings;
- evidence-atom embeddings;
- BM25 indexes;
- ontology adjacency;
- common quantity conversions;
- study lineage;
- common evidence packets where safe/versioned.

Query time performs state-specific filtering/reranking/decision and retrieves exact citations.

## 257A.19 Professor/API integration policy

When professor-provided APIs arrive:

1. inventory endpoints and data definitions;
2. map them to existing internal schemas;
3. do not redesign the ontology merely to mirror API quirks;
4. preserve source IDs/provenance;
5. run overlap/duplicate audits against already acquired sources;
6. update the data-support map and priority queue;
7. freeze a new evidence/data version before experiments.

## 257A.20 Experiment registry template

Every experiment record should include:

```text
experiment_id
research_question_id
hypothesis
code_commit
dataset_version
split_version
schema_version
ontology_version
prompt/model versions
baselines
model config
random seeds
compute
metrics
confidence intervals
artifacts
failure notes
decision: KEEP / MODIFY / DROP / NEED_DATA
next dependency
```

## 257A.21 Result-to-decision rules

```text
POSITIVE:
  promote only if gain survives required cold/source split and uncertainty.

NULL:
  prefer simpler baseline unless another strong benefit (calibration/latency/provenance) exists.

NEGATIVE:
  record and drop/modify architecture; do not hide.

INCONCLUSIVE:
  identify whether cause is data power, label ambiguity, leakage, implementation or model inadequacy.

DATA-LIMITED:
  stop model escalation and acquire/curate evidence.
```

Defer unless core gates pass:

- full POMDP/RL;

## 257A.24 Minimum viable end-to-end scenario

A scientifically credible MVP can be demonstrated with one scenario that exercises the whole chain:

```text
real recipe/session input
→ ingredient + quantity normalization
→ state/event graph
→ user asks process/next-action question
→ state-aware evidence retrieval
→ evidence packet with proof/unknowns
→ direct evidence or gated Level-15 fallback
→ feasible action alternatives
→ confidence/abstention
→ claim-level cited response
→ session state update
```

This is more valuable than a broad but unverifiable chatbot.

## 257A.25 Final implementation sanity checklist

Before calling the course system "complete", verify:

- [ ] raw sources are immutable/versioned;
- [ ] schemas are frozen/versioned;
- [ ] provenance enum is enforced;
- [ ] gold is independently annotated;
- [ ] duplicate/source leakage is controlled;
- [ ] vocabulary coverage and long-tail errors are reported;
- [ ] quantity conversions expose their evidence class;
- [ ] unknown chemistry remains unknown;
- [ ] evidence atoms retain exact proof/source spans;
- [ ] retrieval uses condition/state compatibility;
- [ ] conflict is explicit;
- [ ] confidence is calibrated rather than self-reported;
- [ ] transition model is gated by Level-15 results;
- [ ] actions pass feasibility constraints;
- [ ] diagnosis and recovery evidence are distinct;
- [ ] final claims have a claim ledger;
- [ ] strong baseline/ablation results exist;
- [ ] negative results are recorded;
- [ ] FlavorTwin does not overclaim sensory equivalence;
- [ ] reproducibility metadata is complete;
- [ ] Level 17 remains optional rather than blocking delivery.

# 257B. DETAILED MODULE-BY-MODULE IMPLEMENTATION AND TEST CONTRACTS

This section expands the 18-module registry into implementation contracts. It is intentionally repetitive where repetition creates an auditable engineering checklist.

## 257B.1 C1 — Query/intent parser

**Primary inputs:** raw query + session context.

**Primary outputs:** intent labels, targets, requested mode.

**Implementation obligations:**
- Define a typed input contract and reject malformed/ambiguous records instead of silently coercing them.
- Preserve the raw source/query form in addition to normalized outputs.
- Attach module version, schema version and upstream artifact versions to every persisted result.
- Return explicit UNKNOWN/UNRESOLVED states when information is insufficient.
- Expose machine-readable failure/rejection reasons for debugging and evaluation.
- Avoid performing responsibilities owned by another module merely for convenience.
- Provide deterministic replay on frozen input/model/prompt versions where technically possible.
- Emit provenance/features required by downstream confidence calibration.
- Support oracle-upstream evaluation so downstream performance can be isolated.
- Support predicted-upstream end-to-end evaluation to measure cascade error.

**Unit tests:**
- test clean in-domain case;
- test missing optional fields;
- test missing critical field;
- test ambiguous surface form;
- test contradictory upstream fields;
- test source/locale variation;
- test near-duplicate input;
- test OOD concept/process;
- test explicit UNKNOWN;
- test malformed identifier/reference;
- test version mismatch;
- test round-trip/replay where applicable.

**Evaluation reporting:**
- report micro metric where useful.
- report macro metric across entity/process/source buckets.
- report source-disjoint result.
- report long-tail/frequency-bucket result.
- report error taxonomy.
- report confidence/calibration when probabilistic.
- report latency and cost.
- report human-review burden if used.

**Promotion rule:** the module is promoted only if it improves the relevant downstream or module-specific gate against the strongest simpler baseline; otherwise retain the simpler implementation.

- test missing optional fields;
- test missing critical field;
- test ambiguous surface form;
- test contradictory upstream fields;
- test source/locale variation;
- test near-duplicate input;
- test OOD concept/process;
- test explicit UNKNOWN;
- test malformed identifier/reference;
- test version mismatch;
- test round-trip/replay where applicable.

**Evaluation reporting:**
- report micro metric where useful.
- report macro metric across entity/process/source buckets.
- report source-disjoint result.
- report long-tail/frequency-bucket result.
- report error taxonomy.
- report confidence/calibration when probabilistic.
- report latency and cost.
- report human-review burden if used.

**Promotion rule:** the module is promoted only if it improves the relevant downstream or module-specific gate against the strongest simpler baseline; otherwise retain the simpler implementation.

# 257D. GOLD TEST CATALOG FOR VOCABULARY, QUANTITY, ENTITY, AND STATE PARSING

These are semantic test classes, not a claim that every phrase has an authoritative gram conversion. The expected behavior is often to parse correctly and return UNKNOWN for unsupported conversion.

## 257D.Q001 Quantity case: `1 cup millet`
- Preserve the exact raw phrase and source span.
- Parse scalar/range/fraction/count/unit/size/packing/container/qualifier fields as applicable.
- Resolve locale-sensitive unit only when source/locale evidence is sufficient.
- Perform exact physical conversion only through deterministic unit logic.
- Perform food-specific mass conversion only with a portion/density/empirical record; otherwise mass remains UNKNOWN.
- Preserve state/form distinctions (raw/cooked, chopped/whole, melted/solid, packed/loose) because density/portion can change.
- Validator must reject silent midpoint substitution for ranges and silent numericization of qualitative quantities.

# 257E. EXPANDED RESEARCH-PROTOCOL TEMPLATE FOR ALL RQ16 QUESTIONS

Every RQ16 experiment must complete the following protocol before code is run. This prevents architecture-first experimentation and makes negative results actionable.

## 257E.1 Protocol for RQ16-01 Semantic state value
- **Scientific claim under test:** rewrite the RQ as one falsifiable claim; avoid claims broader than the available population/domain.
- **Unit of analysis:** define recipe, ingredient mention, evidence query, study, transition pair, session or user decision as appropriate.
- **Population/domain:** state source languages/locales, food/process families and evidence tiers included.
- **Data inclusion:** freeze criteria before viewing final test results.
- **Data exclusion:** document missing/invalid/provenance exclusions; do not exclude hard cases after failure.
- **Target definition:** define exact label/measurement and evidence precision.
- **Baseline hierarchy:** run the cheapest credible null/simple baselines first.
- **Proposed model:** specify only the component required to test the hypothesis.
- **Confounds:** list source/template/frequency/ingredient/process/condition/duplicate/measurement effects.
- **Split:** choose group-safe/source/cold/OOD split matched to the claim.
- **Leakage audit:** verify duplicates, source lineage, outcome phrases and external retrieval cannot leak the held-out target unless the experiment is explicitly RAG retrieval.
- **Metrics:** include macro/per-bucket metrics and uncertainty/confidence intervals.
- **Calibration:** if probabilistic/abstaining, reserve calibration data and report risk–coverage.
- **Seeds/repeats:** specify repeated seeds or grouped bootstrap as appropriate.
- **Compute budget:** set an evaluation/optimization budget so models/search methods are comparable.
- **Ablation:** identify the minimum ablation that proves the claimed component matters.
- **Oracle test:** if cascade system, test with oracle upstream inputs.
- **Error taxonomy:** predefine categories for qualitative error analysis.
- **Success gate:** define what result would promote the method.
- **Null gate:** define what result causes retention of the simpler baseline.
- **Negative gate:** define what result causes DROP/MODIFY/NEED_DATA.
- **External validity:** state what populations/processes the result does not justify.
- **Provenance:** freeze dataset/split/schema/ontology/model/prompt/code versions.
- **Decision record:** record KEEP / MODIFY / DROP / NEED_DATA and the next dependency.

# 257F. SOURCE ACQUISITION AND EVIDENCE-CURATION PROTOCOLS

## 257F.1 Recipe sources

For each recipe corpus/source capture:

- source/dataset name and version;
- URL or persistent identifier where allowed;
- licensing/terms and redistribution status;
- language/locale;
- source-domain/template ID;
- raw-text availability;
- ingredient/instruction/serving fields;
- existing IDs/metadata;
- known duplicates/lineage;
- acquisition date/checksum.

## 257F.2 Food composition / portion sources

Capture whether a source provides:

- canonical food description;
- state/form;
- household portion;
- gram weight;
- density;
- edible portion;
- preparation notes;
- country/locale;
- source provenance;
- version/date.

Do not merge portion values across states/forms/locales until compatibility is established.

## 257F.3 Scientific process-effect papers

Before extraction, record study-level metadata:

- food species/variety/matrix;
- raw/pretreated state;
- process/equipment;
- condition ranges;
- target compounds/properties;
- analytical platform;
- replicate/sample structure;
- table/figure availability;
- study design/control;
- DOI/source;
- source quality/evidence tier.

## 257F.4 Table extraction

For every extracted table cell retain:

- row header;
- column header;
- value;
- unit;
- basis/normalization;
- footnote markers;
- table caption;
- study ID;
- exact cell/row locator if possible;
- extraction method;
- human verification status.

## 257F.5 Figure digitization

When a result exists only in a plot:

- preserve original figure reference;
- store digitization tool/version;
- store approximate extraction uncertainty;
- label value DIGITIZED;
- never silently merge digitized values with exact tabular values without a quality flag.

## 257F.6 Mechanism/review evidence

Review papers can support mechanism/background and source discovery. They should not automatically replace the primary quantitative experiment when the primary source is available.

## 257F.7 Evidence conflict protocol

Create a conflict record only after compatibility checks. The record includes supporting sets, opposing sets, matched variables, differing conditions/platforms, independent-source count and unresolved explanation.


# 257G. DATASET AUDIT REPORT — REQUIRED TABLES FOR EVERY MAJOR RELEASE

Each release report must include the following blocks.

## 257G.1 Source distribution

- total recipes;
- unique source domains;
- recipes per source;
- top-source concentration;
- source-disjoint split counts;
- duplicate groups per source and cross-source;
- license/release eligibility counts.

## 257G.2 Linguistic/locale distribution

- languages;
- locales/measurement systems;
- regional alias counts;
- unresolved locale-sensitive units;
- transliteration/non-ASCII term counts.

## 257G.3 Recipe complexity

- ingredients per recipe distribution;
- steps/events per recipe;
- intermediate entities;
- graph nodes/edges;
- merge/split/reserve/discard/recombine frequencies;
- coreference instances;
- qualitative endpoint frequency.

## 257G.4 Vocabulary coverage

- canonical ingredient concepts;
- aliases;
- mentions mapped exact/alias/hierarchical/ambiguous/unmapped;
- coverage by frequency decile;
- coverage by source/locale;
- top unresolved phrases;
- concept merge/split changes since prior version.

## 257G.5 Quantity coverage

- ingredient mentions with explicit quantity;
- numeric/range/fraction/count/qualitative proportions;
- resolved physical units;
- locale-ambiguous units;
- authoritative portion conversions;
- density-based conversions;
- empirical distribution conversions;
- model estimates;
- unknown mass/volume rate;
- conversion outliers/review queue.

## 257G.6 Process/state coverage

- canonical process counts;
- process-family distribution;
- states/forms/tools;
- duration coverage;
- temperature coverage;
- pH/water-activity/pressure coverage;
- endpoint phrase distribution;
- unknown-state field rates.

## 257G.7 Annotation quality

- Deep-Gold IAA by field/task;
- Silver vs Gold field F1;
- graph errors;
- provenance violations;
- automatic validator failure rate;
- reannotation rate;
- human review rate;
- cost per accepted record.

## 257G.8 Scientific evidence support

- evidence atoms by target/process/food;
- direct vs near/model/simulated counts;
- study/source independence;
- condition coverage;
- target/compound coverage;
- conflict clusters;
- human-verified fraction;
- unsupported query-space analysis.

## 257G.9 Split integrity

- train/validation/calibration/test counts;
- duplicate groups crossing splits (must be zero under policy);
- source groups crossing source-disjoint split (must follow design);
- ingredient/process cold counts;
- target leakage audit results.


# 257H. ANNOTATION FEW-SHOT DESIGN REQUIREMENTS

Few-shot examples should teach the policy boundaries, not merely easy formatting.

## 257H.1 Example class — clean ingredient

Input:
```text
2 tomatoes, chopped
```
Expected conceptual structure:
```text
food=tomato
count=2
form=chopped
mass=UNKNOWN unless portion evidence is separately invoked
```
Forbidden shortcut: inventing a gram mass from general knowledge.

## 257H.2 Example class — quantity + container

Input:
```text
1 (14 oz) can diced tomatoes
```
Expected conceptual structure:
```text
food=tomato
form=diced
container=can
container stated mass=14 oz raw expression
normalize physical mass deterministically if unit conversion requested
```
Do not assume drained mass or edible mass unless source/portion evidence states it.

## 257H.3 Example class — ambiguous word

Input contexts:
```text
3 cloves garlic
1/4 tsp ground cloves
```
The first uses a garlic portion/count; the second uses clove spice. Context resolves identity/quantity roles.

## 257H.4 Example class — split/reserve

Input:
```text
Mix the sauce. Reserve half. Add half of the reserved sauce later.
```
Expected behavior: create split entities/allocations, preserve the reserved branch and use the correct descendant later.

## 257H.5 Example class — endpoint without numeric condition

Input:
```text
Bake until golden.
```
Expected:
```text
process=BAKE
endpoint_state=golden
time=UNKNOWN
temperature=UNKNOWN unless specified elsewhere
```

## 257H.6 Example class — chemistry firewall

Input:
```text
Boil the broccoli for 8 minutes.
```
Expected procedural annotation does not invent vitamin retention, pH or compound concentrations. Scientific enrichment is a separate query/evidence process.

## 257H.7 Example class — conflicting source

If source ingredient list says 2 eggs but instruction says add 3 eggs, preserve both source statements and flag conflict; do not silently choose 2 or 3.

## 257H.8 Example class — user observation overrides prediction

If prior model state predicted `light_brown` and user explicitly reports `black`, current observable color becomes user-observed black with timestamp/provenance; prior prediction remains in audit history.


# 257I. SOFTWARE TEST STRATEGY AND CONTINUOUS DATA VALIDATION

## 257I.1 Test layers

```text
unit tests
schema tests
property-based quantity/unit tests
golden semantic examples
graph replay tests
retrieval regression tests
calibration regression tests
end-to-end scenario tests
data-release audits
```

## 257I.2 Property-based quantity tests

Generate mathematically equivalent expressions and verify identical canonical physical results when the unit is exact. Examples: kg↔g, L↔mL, °C↔°F when only temperature representation changes. Do not enforce invariance for ambiguous locale-dependent culinary portions without resolved locale.

## 257I.3 Graph replay tests

Given a frozen event sequence, reconstruct the same current state deterministically. If annotation corrections change upstream events, a new graph/data version should yield the expected revised state.

## 257I.4 Retrieval regression tests

Maintain a small fixed suite of evidence queries with expected gold evidence IDs/hard negatives. Reranker/index changes cannot silently destroy retrieval quality.

## 257I.5 Prompt regression tests

Every new LLM prompt/model version runs against the same hard Gold subset. Compare field-level and graph-level changes before production reannotation.

## 257I.6 Data-contract tests

A release fails if required provenance, source checksum, split registry or schema versions are missing even when model metrics are high.


# 257J. USER-FACING BEHAVIOR AND HUMAN-AGENCY CONTRACT

The system should be useful without pretending certainty.

## 257J.1 Response layers

Preferred answer structure:

1. direct action/finding;
2. concise reason;
3. evidence status/uncertainty when material;
4. optional deeper chemistry/mechanism;
5. citations/provenance for scientific claims.

## 257J.2 Trade-offs

When objectives conflict, present alternatives tied to explicit priorities rather than choosing a hidden preference.

## 257J.3 Clarification

Ask only when the missing observation can materially change the recommendation. Avoid questionnaire behavior.

## 257J.4 Honest limitation

When evidence is sparse, downgrade precision or abstain rather than filling gaps with plausible-sounding culinary knowledge.

## 257J.5 FlavorTwin language

Use terms such as chemical-profile similarity, descriptor similarity, structural similarity or model-estimated process-conditioned match according to actual evidence. Reserve human flavor-equivalence language for sensory validation.


# 257K. IMPLEMENTATION SEQUENCING CHECKLIST FOR A SEMESTER-SCALE PROJECT

The exact calendar can be adapted, but the dependency order should remain.

## Block 1 — contracts and gold seed
- freeze v0 schemas;
- freeze provenance classes;
- seed unit/process/state vocabularies;
- annotate first difficult gold recipes;
- implement validators.

## Block 2 — quantity/vocabulary engine
- alias registry;
- canonicalization queue;
- exact unit conversions;
- authoritative portion imports where permitted;
- quantity parser benchmark.

## Block 3 — 10k pilot
- multi-pass LLM annotation;
- audit;
- duplicate grouping;
- source distribution;
- cost/quality report;
- prompt/schema repair.

## Block 4 — semantic graph + parser
- event parsing;
- coreference;
- intermediate entities;
- merge/split;
- state replay;
- Gold evaluation.

## Block 5 — evidence/RAG baseline
- evidence atom store;
- BM25/dense/structured retrieval;
- strong B1–B3 baselines;
- compatible retrieval benchmark.

## Block 6 — state-aware RAG
- query-state reconstruction;
- evidence packet compiler;
- B4/B5 evaluation;
- claim ledger.

## Block 7 — calibration/decision
- held-out calibration;
- abstention;
- feasibility/action schema;
- B6/B7 comparison.

## Block 8 — integration and paper/demo
- locked final test;
- ablations;
- decision record;
- demo scenarios;
- course report/paper draft.

FlavorTwin process-conditioned implementation runs after the shared state/evidence core is stable, unless the course specifically prioritizes it earlier.

# 257L. RESEARCH-QUESTION EXECUTION FLOW — DECISION-MAKING PROCEDURE FOR ALL RQ16 EXPERIMENTS

This section operationalizes the 30 RQs as a common research workflow. It is deliberately detailed so a code/research agent can execute one question without reconstructing the methodology from chat.

## 257L.1 Execution card — RQ16-01 Semantic state value

### A. Claim freeze
Write one sentence that can be false. Specify the exact population, unit of analysis and target. Do not use words such as better, robust or general without defining the metric/domain.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### B. Data support audit
Count eligible examples, groups, sources, classes/targets, missingness and duplicates. If the target is not supported at the intended fidelity, downgrade the claim before modeling.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### C. Gold/evidence status
State which labels are independent human gold, source-measured evidence, Silver, imputed, simulated or model-estimated. Final headline evaluation uses the allowed real/gold regime only.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### D. Confound register
List source template, popularity/frequency, recipe size, cuisine/locale, ingredient identity, process, temperature/time, analytical platform, duplicate family and annotation-model effects relevant to this RQ.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### E. Baseline freeze
Run the simplest null plus the strongest simple baseline before tuning the proposed method. Store baseline artifacts and splits.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### F. Split freeze
Choose duplicate-safe and claim-relevant source/cold/OOD groups. Freeze split IDs before final tuning.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### G. Leakage audit
Check target text leakage, endpoint phrases, near duplicates, source-derived copies, label-in-input, retrieval of held-out outcome and calibration/test contamination.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### H. Proposed method
Add only the component necessary to answer the RQ. Do not bundle unrelated architecture changes into one comparison.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### I. Hyperparameter budget
Set comparable search/evaluation budget across methods. Record search space and selection metric.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### J. Calibration
If the model returns probabilities/intervals or abstains, reserve calibration data distinct from the final test.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### K. Primary metric
Declare one or a small set of primary metrics tied directly to the RQ before viewing final test results.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### L. Secondary metrics
Include calibration, cost, latency, coverage, provenance violations or constraint errors when they affect system usefulness.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
- [ ] no unverified synthetic/imputed final targets;
- [ ] result interpreted within evidence precision.

### M. Macro/subgroup reporting
Report per food/process/source/frequency/locale or support regime where appropriate; do not let common classes hide failures.

Checklist:
- [ ] decision recorded before final test where applicable;
- [ ] artifacts/version IDs attached;
